featured_reviews.name: Ishita Soni
featured_reviews.review_text:
If there’s one place in Mumbai that quietly sets the bar ridiculously high for café dining, it has to be Journal.

Tucked in the lanes of Santacruz West, this spot feels like a hidden gem that you almost want to gatekeep — but it’s too good not to talk about.

Let’s start with the food — because wow.
I tried the Rigatoni Romesco pasta, and I’m not exaggerating when I say it has redefined what a good pasta should taste like for me. Perfectly cooked, rich, and balanced — the kind of dish you keep thinking about days later. The grilled artichoke & mushroom pizza was equally incredible — earthy, flavourful, and done just right.

What makes Journal stand out is that the food isn’t just good — it’s consistently thoughtful. The menu spans across multiple healthy and cheat options, so there’s always something exciting to try.  ￼
And nothing feels like filler — even the simplest dishes feel well-crafted.

The space itself adds so much charm to the experience. You’ve got both indoor and outdoor seating, and the outdoor section especially makes for a perfect brunch vibe. It’s relaxed, airy, and yes — there are quite a few cats casually strolling around, which somehow just adds to the whole personality of the place.

The vibe is exactly what you want from a café — calm, slightly buzzy, and very “slow morning energy.” It’s spacious, comfortable, and great whether you’re working, catching up, or just unwinding.  ￼

And the coffee? Absolutely holds its own. Smooth, well-brewed, and clearly taken seriously — which makes sense given it positions itself as a space for “coffee, culture & conversations.”  ￼

Service is warm and easy — the kind where you don’t feel rushed, and everything just flows.

Overall, Journal isn’t just a café — it’s an experience. One where the food genuinely impresses, the vibe grows on you, and you end up staying longer than planned.

If you’re someone who appreciates great food, good coffee, cozy corners, and a slow brunch done right — this one is an absolute must-visit.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Absolutely one of my favorite Starbucks spots – perfect balance of bold coffee and delightful treats!
I recently stopped by this Starbucks outlet and had one of the best experiences in a while. The vibe was cozy and welcoming, staff were super friendly and quick, and the place was spotless – always a plus.
For my drink, I went for a Vietnamese-style iced coffee hack that's become my go-to obsession here: a quad shot iced espresso (four bold shots for that intense kick) with 3-4 pumps of white mocha syrup, extra ice, and topped with a generous layer of sweet vanilla cream cold foam. It nails that rich, creamy, sweet-yet-strong flavor profile of authentic Vietnamese cà phê sữa đá – the condensed milk sweetness without actually using condensed milk. It's dangerously addictive, super refreshing on a warm day, and hits way harder than a standard latte. If you're into bold, Southeast Asian-inspired coffee vibes, ask the barista to make this custom – they know exactly what to do and it comes out perfect every time. Absolute game-changer!
To pair with it, I grabbed a slice of the Orange Almond Cake (the Valencia Orange one). Oh man, where do I even start? This thing is moist, dense in the best way, packed with real orange pulp and zest for that bright, citrusy punch, and loaded with crunchy almonds on top and throughout. The almond flavor complements the orange beautifully – nutty, slightly sweet, and not overly sugary. It's got that homemade feel with clean ingredients, and honestly, it feels indulgent yet almost wholesome. One slice with the strong coffee was the perfect afternoon pick-me-up; the citrus cuts through the richness of the drink like magic.
Everything was fresh, flavorful, and made with care. Prices felt fair for the quality, and the whole combo left me smiling long after I left. If this outlet keeps delivering like this, it'll stay on my regular rotation. Highly recommend swinging by for the Vietnamese coffee hack + orange almond cake combo – you won't regret it!

featured_reviews.review_text:
Boulevard is one of the famous restaurant since ages. Orchid can be easily said to be one of the best ecotel hotel since years. Buffet of them had really lot of options. View from the restaurant is excellent too. Certainly a must visit restaurant if you want to enjoy the lavish spread. Strongly recommend, go for it.

Location- This restaurant is on the first floor of very famous ecotel hotel Orchid. Orchid is just adjacent to the domestic airport.(5/5)

Theme- Being the main restaurant of the hotel it's 24*7, it serves mix cuisine with a la carte and buffet both.(5/5)

Ambience- one side of first floor is occupied by this restaurant so yes it's really big. Divided into small sections. You can get a lobby view from any table.  One side of restaurant they got lovely spreaded buffet . Lighting is bright n fresh. Got mix tables or 2,4,8 covers. Soft music at background was nice.(5/5)

Food- This being a main restaurant of the hotel, it is open 24*7. You either can go for a la carte menu or decide to go with the lavish buffet spread. We decided to hog on buffet which looked really impressive.  Buffet consist of soup, salads, farsaan,starters, Chaat counter, main courses, desserts.(5/5)

Soup was the first dish I tastes and was highly impressive with the taste of it. It was seafood clear soup which was made with fish stock, fish chunks, thick sliced celery. Great way to start.
Chaat counter had various options like seven Puri, dahi Puri, dahi wada, bhel. You have to order your dish to the chef who was standing on the counter and he will send it to your table.
I had a go at dahi Puri which was delicious.

Starters they had paneer Tikka, corn bruschetta, fish fingers, chicken in Asian style. Fish finger was the dish I kept eating for long, fresh fish and crispy enough.

Salad counter had mix of veg and nonveg salads, loved the smoked salmon salad and tuna potato salad.
Very rare that I saw a farsaan options in multicuisine restaurant of 5*. They were serving bakerwadi and khokla, I didn't try it though was looking tempting.
Same section had options of nachos with in-house cheese sauce.

Main course really had many options. Pasta  live counter seemed very busy. I opted for more Indian food as awadhi gosht korma caught my attention. Excellent colour with medium thickness gravy and well cooked lamb in it was heaven with the butter naan (any bread options you like) which they serve on table.
Dishes like Pan seared fish with garlic cilantro butter sauce, chicken in black bean sauce were a must try.
Coming to rice , I saw Chicken biryani  first time itself when was checking the buffet. So took biryani with some for a gravy. Biryani was well made with long grain rice, garnished well with fried onions and had extraordinary aroma of it's own, Enjoyed it.

Dessert section is always said to be the best part of any buffet, it's true. Here they had mix if Indian and continental desserts. Had dark chocolate mousse, kiwi mousse, peach apricot jelly, Chocolate mud cake , strawberry salsa with caramel mousse etc. Had ice cream options along with black current Halwa and kesari kheer.
